candidates.snippet: The later years of the Peloponnesian War witnessed much mental disturbance and restlessness at Athens. More than at any time since the age of Cleisthenes, the city was divided, and a man’s foes were often men of his own tribe or deme. Contention in the law courts and rivalries in the assembly had for many men a more Antecedent Conditions. absorbing interest than questions of peace and war. Hereditary traditions had relaxed their hold, and political principles were not yet formulated.
